section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a single study (Study X) that investigated the prevalence and correlates of loneliness among 2025 older U.S. veterans (aged 60 and older) from a nationally representative sample. The study found that 44% of veterans reported feeling lonely at least some of the time. Key findings indicated that dispositional gratitude, social support, and secure attachment were negatively associated with loneliness, while greater age, disability, trauma, stress, and depressive symptoms were positively associated. The authors suggest multifactorial interventions focusing on social support and reducing depressive symptoms to mitigate loneliness in this population.
